_note: Part landing pages. Titles are the \part titles of docs/book/main.tex. Summaries are drafted from each Part's opening chapter, in plain words, with no claim the book does not make; 'referee' says what a reader in that field should check first. Edit freely.

parts.label: part:1
parts.summary: Part I states IAM's Law: every irreversible step from a quantum superposition to a classical record costs at least k_B T ln 2 per bit, paid at the temperature of the nearest encoding surface, and the record is written on that surface. Its opening chapter follows one condition, floor breach, from a black hole to a cell, and its last chapters set out the virial partition: a stable 1/r system holds half its binding energy as motion, and that half is the irreversible cost of binding.
parts.referee: Check the six-step derivation of the opening chapter, which says that only Step 5 is a new identification, and the virial-half argument that the later Parts build on.

parts.label: part:2
parts.summary: Part II applies the virial half to the universe: it fixes the coupling of the record term in the horizon first law, beta_m = Omega_m/2 = 0.15765, with no free parameter. The single term beta_m E(a), with E(a) = exp(1 - 1/a) from horizon thermodynamics, enters the matter-sector perturbation equations only, and the background expansion is left unchanged. The chapters derive the growth coupling, the two expansion rates and the amplitude of structure, and compare them with Planck chains, distance and growth data.
parts.referee: Check the coupling derivation of the first chapter, which every later chapter uses, and the chain records behind the two H0 values (67.16 photon sector, 72.26 matter sector).

parts.label: part:bh
parts.summary: Part III reads the same law at a black hole, where the nearest encoding surface is the horizon itself at the Hawking temperature. Starting from the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy and the Hawking temperature, it derives the encoding throughput, shows that the Stefan-Boltzmann luminosity of the horizon and the black-body Hawking luminosity are one formula, and prices the horizon's bits, where the Smarr half appears.
parts.referee: Check the horizon thermodynamics against the cited foundations (Bekenstein, Hawking, Jacobson, Cai and Kim) and the step where Landauer's principle is applied to the horizon.

parts.label: part:qp
parts.summary: Part IV follows the law down to where records begin, the quantum-to-classical transition, and back up to the cosmic ledger E(a) as the sum of those transitions. It takes Zurek's account of decoherence and quantum Darwinism for how records form, IAM's Law for what each record costs and where it is written, and gravitational collapse for how fast records are written. It then reads measurement, gravitational decoherence, the electroweak record, the lepton masses and the electron mass in the same terms.
parts.referee: Check where the book separates established decoherence physics from its own identification, and the numbers it compares with laboratory bounds.

parts.label: part:3
parts.summary: Part V gives the physics and the concept of how a qubit or a transistor sits against its own floor, set by k_B T ln 2 at its own temperature. It treats the superconducting qubit's tunnel barrier as an encoding surface, then the quasiparticle background, the coherence optimum, the main qubit platforms, and CMOS logic across chip generations. Numbers for real processors are the makers' own published values, cited where used.
parts.referee: Check that each device number matches its cited source and that the floor is applied at the right temperature for each platform.

parts.label: part:4
parts.summary: Part VI reads the methylome the way cosmology reads the sky: one cell read against a calibrated reference, to say how far it sits from where it should be. Its physical claim is that the cost that governs an encoding surface in cosmology governs the methylation record too, with the per-site holding energy, the floor and the Mahaffey number of the cell set from k_B T ln 2 at body temperature. The chapters build the instrument and report its first readings.
parts.referee: Check the holding-energy and floor derivations, the frozen references the instrument reads against, and the committed readings behind each reported number.

parts.label: part:5
parts.summary: Part VII joins the scales. It sets out the nine-step chain from gravitational collapse to decoherence, the Landauer cost, holographic encoding and the feedback on expansion, and marks which steps are established physics and which are the framework's conjecture. It then reads time, the virial partners, one gauge across the scales, the predictions, the open problems and the status of every claim.
parts.referee: Check the line the book draws between established physics (steps 1-5) and its conjecture (steps 6-9), and the predictions and their status table.
